purpose: CPU cost of secret redaction per chunk (ADR 0060): always-on rules and opt-in OpenAI Privacy Filter
cpu: 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HX (8P+16E cores, 32 threads)
corpus: this checkout's tracked .py/.go/.md/.ts/.tsx/.json/.yml/.toml files, cut into consecutive 1,000/2,000/4,000-character chunks
conditions: Shared workstation: other agents' test runs and browsers were active. Load average 1.2-4.9 during the 'linux_low_load' run and 2-8 during the others. Single-shot rule timings are bimodal (about 5% of chunks at 10-14 ms) from scheduling; the slowest chunks take about 0.5 ms when timed best of 5, so medians are the representative figure.

model.file: onnx/model_q4f16.onnx (809,061,992 bytes of external data) + tokenizer.json (27,868,174 bytes)

linux_low_load.platform: Linux x86_64 under WSL2, Python 3.12.8, onnxruntime 1.31.0 (CPU)

linux_model_load.note: Each load verifies three SHA-256 digests (about 2 s warm for the weights) and creates the session (3-4 s).

windows_native.platform: Windows 11 x64, the installed runtime's Python 3.12.8, onnxruntime-gpu 1.31.0 with CPUExecutionProvider
windows_native.smoke_redaction: The vault password is [REDACTED:secret], my IBAN is [REDACTED:account-number], ask Harry Potter.
windows_native.note: Run from a temporary copy of imprint/ with a temporary IMPRINT_DATA_DIR; the installation's config and data were not touched. Chunks were sampled from the same corpus definition after documentation edits, so token counts differ slightly from the Linux sample.

export_comparison_single_pass_1024_token.note: Random token ids, one pass, best of two; measured before the corpus runs at lower machine load.

q4f16_sequence_length_threads_4.note: One pass of random token ids. Longer passes grow superlinearly in time and memory; Imprint labels windows of 1,024 tokens plus 128 tokens of context each side (1,280).

rules_findings_in_corpus: Two values in 6,665/3,211/1,481 chunks at the final run (a TOKEN constant in each of two test files); the earlier run also redacted a URL password in a test fixture that a later rule change treats as a placeholder word. No finding in non-test code.

real_model_smoke.linux: tests/test_redaction.py RealPrivacyFilterSmokeTests passed offline with IMPRINT_TEST_PRIVACY_FILTER_DATA: names and email kept, password and IBAN redacted, redacting again changed nothing.
real_model_smoke.windows: The vault password is [REDACTED:secret], my IBAN is [REDACTED:account-number], ask Harry Potter.

embedding_comparison_threads_4.note: The paired run overlapped load averages of 5-13 from other workloads, which inflates both absolute times; the ratio is the comparable figure.

privacy_filter_on_test_corpora.false_positive_corpus: 3 of 22 texts got spans: a UUID and a SHA-256 hex digest (as account-number) and the placeholder password in 'postgres://app:secret@localhost/db'. The rules flag none of the 22.
privacy_filter_on_test_corpora.rule_true_positives: No span in 8 of 28 texts, mostly bare tokens in a synthetic 'value <token> end' context (AWS, GitLab, OpenAI, Anthropic, Slack webhook, npm, PyPI) and a redis URL password. The rules redact all 28.
privacy_filter_on_test_corpora.repository_chunks: No span in 40 sampled 2,000-character chunks of this repository.
